newsitem.title: USA: Burn victim Betty Shabazz suffers medical setback.
newsitem.headline: Burn victim Betty Shabazz suffers medical setback.

text.p: The widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, who was badly burned in a fire allegedly set by her grandson, has suffered "serious medical problems" in recent days, hospital officials said Wednesday.

"In the last 24 to 48 hours, Betty Shabazz has been experiencing serious medical problems that are typical of a severe burn injury of this magnitude," said a spokeswoman at the Jacobi Medical Centre burn unit where Shabazz was being treated for third degree burns.
The hospital declined to reveal the nature of the problems but said they were "clearly of a life-threatening nature. Her condition remains extremely critical."
Shabazz has had five surgical procedures to remove and replace about 85 percent of her charred skin after her body was set on fire in her Yonkers, N.Y., apartment June 1.
During the operations, her burned skin was replaced with Integra, an artifical skin product that helps the inner layer of skin heal enough to accept a permanent skin graft later.

"The biggest risk at this time is from infection because the patient's immune system is compromised and can't fight off infection," Dr. Roger Yurt, director of the burn unit at New York-Cornell Medical Centre said.
He said it was life-threatening was because the body must gear up to do twice as much work, which puts a tremendous demand on such vital organs as the heart, kidneys and lungs.
Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, is accused of splashing gasoline at the door of his grandmother's apartment and allegedly setting it on fire.
The boy was living with her because his mother, Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, was concerned about the company he was keeping at her San Antonio, Texas, home.
